D=rho halftrace norm; SEP=all heterogeneous product mixtures. Put beta=log(1+1/nu_N),b_N=beta sqrtN→1/c; independent E_j~Exp(pi²j²), S=sum E_j (ES=1/6), mu=lawS. H_N(A,b)=exp(−A J²/N−b Jz/sqrtN), Z_N=2^-N TrH_N, eta_N=H_N/(2^N Z_N). Euler product gives EXACT rho_N=integral eta_N(sb_N²,b_N) W_N(ds), W_N=C_beta e^-s beta²/4 Z_N(sb_N²,b_N)mu(ds), C_beta=sinh(beta/2)/(beta/2). Density tends inL1 to K_b(s)=(1+s b²/2)^-3/2 exp[b²/(8+4s b²)].
For0<A<1, iid uniform unitR_i,U=sumR_i/sqrtN,omega(R)=(I+R·sigma)/2; alpha=9A/[4(1−A)],h=−3b/[2(1−A)], sigma_N(A,b)=E[e^-alpha|U|²+hUz tensor_i omega(R_i)]/E[e^-alpha|U|²+hUz]. Explicit FULLSEP, heterogeneous pure factors with correlated classical weights. Three normalized-tracial-L² limits H²,Q²,HQ (or paired orientation squared norm) imply D(eta_N,sigma_N)→0, stronger than weak CLT. Fourier local factor norm<=1→Gaussian convolution exp(−A|x|²−bz). Replace mixture part sb_N²>=1 byI/2^N to obtain Sigma_N.
limsup D(rho_N,Sigma_N)<=delta(c)=integral_{s>=c²} K_{1/c}(s)mu(ds)<=min{1,2(2/3)^3/2 exp(−pi²c²+1/(12c²))}; delta~2(2/3)^3/2e^-pi²c² as c→∞ AFTER N→∞. Atc1 quadrature delta≈5.818971380680e-5, analyticbound6.12026e-5 (identity comparator .18963665). Discarded mass is an UPPER error, not entanglement lower/exact optimum.

----------------------------------
Let tau_N(B)=2^(-N) Tr B and X_N=J/sqrt N. Let beta_N=log(1+1/nu_N),
b_N=beta_N sqrt N. The inherited stationary-sector formula implies exactly
  2^N rho_N = exp(-beta_N J_z) h_beta_N(J^2),
  h_beta(j)=(2j+1)/Z_j(beta),
  Z_j(beta)=sinh[(2j+1)beta/2]/sinh(beta/2).
Euler's product (NIST DLMF 4.36.1) gives
  u/sinh u = product_{n>=1} (1+u^2/(pi^2 n^2))^(-1)
           = E exp(-S u^2).
Because (2j+1)^2/4=j(j+1)+1/4, functional calculus gives the EXACT identity
  2^N rho_N = C_beta integral exp[-s beta_N^2/4]
                       exp[-s beta_N^2 J^2-beta_N J_z] mu(ds),
  C_beta=sinh(beta_N/2)/(beta_N/2).
Define
  H_N(A,b)=exp[-A J^2/N-b J_z/sqrt N],
  Z_N(A,b)=tau_N H_N(A,b),
  eta_N(A,b)=H_N(A,b)/(2^N Z_N(A,b)).
Then rho_N is exactly the positive mixture of eta_N(s b_N^2,b_N) with
  W_N(ds)=C_beta exp[-s beta_N^2/4] Z_N(s b_N^2,b_N) mu(ds).
W_N is a probability measure by taking traces of the exact identity.

Under tau_N, j/sqrt N has Maxwell density
  f_r(r)=8 sqrt(2/pi) r^2 exp(-2r^2), r>0,
and m/sqrt N conditional on r becomes Uniform[-r,r]. Therefore
  Z_N(A,b) -> integral_{R^3} G(x) exp[-A|x|^2-bz] dx
            = K(A,b),
  G(x)=(2/pi)^(3/2) exp(-2|x|^2),
  K(A,b)=(1+A/2)^(-3/2) exp[b^2/(8+4A)].
This Riemann-sum limit follows from the inherited Maxwell local CLT, or
directly from binomial multiplicities. For all s>=0, uniformly when b_N bounded,

1. Exact rejection sampler for each pure-product ensemble
---------------------------------------------------------
For 0<A<1, b fixed, draw N iid uniform R_i on S^2, compute
U_N=sum R_i/sqrt N, and accept with probability
  p_A(U_N)/p_max,
  p_A(u)=exp[-alpha|u|^2+h u_z],
  alpha=9A/[4(1-A)], h=-3b/[2(1-A)],
  p_max=exp[h^2/(4alpha)]=exp[b^2/(4A(1-A))].
Upon acceptance, prepare the N pure qubits omega(R_i). This samples exactly
the mathematical sigma_N(A,b) ensemble. No rejected proposal needs physical
qubits prepared; the rejection work is classical.
The expected number of proposals is exactly
  M_N(A,b)=p_max/E p_A(U_N).
Since E|U_N|^2=1 and E(U_N)_z=0, Jensen gives E p>=exp(-alpha), hence the
explicit finite-N bound
  M_N(A,b)<=exp[b^2/(4A(1-A))+9A/(4(1-A))].
This bound is loose but holds for every N. From the scalar CLT normalizer in
the report one obtains the sharper asymptotic value
  M_N(A,b)->[(1+A/2)/(1-A)]^(3/2)
                exp[b^2/(2A(2+A))].
As A approaches0 the limiting cost can be exponential in b^2/A. As A
approaches1 it diverges as (1-A)^(-3/2) times exp(b^2/6). Neither endpoint
is assigned an uncharged ideal sampler.
Each classical proposal costs N sphere samples and O(N) arithmetic; accepted
output costs N pure-qubit preparations. Bit precision and mixture selection
are additional costs, detailed below. There is no entangling preparation step.

2. Endpoint truncation for a finite accuracy target
---------------------------------------------------
Choose a in (0,1/2). Use only components A=s b_N^2 in [a,1-a], and replace
all remaining components by the maximally mixed product state. The resulting
state is exactly FULLSEP for every N and has asymptotic error upper bound
  delta_a(c)=integral_{s outside [a c^2,(1-a)c^2]} K_{1/c}(s)mu(ds).
By continuity and absence of atoms, delta_a(c)->delta(c) as a->0. The
extra sacrificed good-component mass is exactly
  delta_a(c)-delta(c)
     =integral_[0,a c^2) K mu + integral_((1-a)c^2,c^2) K mu.
Thus an arbitrarily small additive epsilon is achievable by an explicit
one-dimensional choice of a, at a cost that must be paid in the sampler.
